text:
Reprints 
U.S. stock indexes stumbled midday Thursday, as the major indexes sank further under their 50-day moving averages. 
X The Dow Jones industrial average led the losers with a 1.5% dent. The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 followed, scrapping off 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively. The small-cap Russell 2000 lost 1.2%. 
Volume in the stock market today was running lower on the NYSE but higher on the Nasdaq vs. the same time in the previous session. 
Most leaders were losing ground, and a few suffered chart damage. Chip equipment maker Ichor Holdings ( ICHR ) dived almost 10% as it pierced its 200-day moving average line in heavy volume. The small-cap stock had already triggered a sell signal after it fell more than 8% from its 33.09 buy point. 
After Wednesday's close, Ichor reported a 40% earnings gain in Q4 on a 39% jump in revenue. 
Among 197 industry groups, the chip equipment group has fallen from No. 25 about two months ago to 93 going into Thursday's session. 
Chart damage also was apparent for apparel maker Canada Goose ( GOOS ). The small-cap stock gapped down 16% before finding support at its 50-day line. 
Canada Goose fell despite reporting a 38% increase in earnings and 27% in revenue in fiscal Q3 ended in December. The Street is expecting fiscal 2018 earnings to drop 34%. 
In the S&P 500, cigarette maker Philip Morris ( PM ) led with a 2.8% gain. 
In the Dow Jones industrial average, Apple ( AAPL ) led the 30-component index with a 0.4% gain. Apple is trading near its 200-day line after losing the 50-day line Jan. 25. 
Meanwhile, the Innovator IBD 50 Fund ( FFTY ) dropped 2.2% in quiet volume. The exchange-traded fund tracks the IBD 50. Innovator IBD 50 gained 37% in 2017, but is down 4% so far this year.
